**4B.4 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador (2024)**

**Bottom line:** negative overall. I found only limited, indirect positive evidence that independent institutions still constrained AMLO in specific episodes, but the dominant 2024 record is the opposite: judicial overhaul, attacks on the INE, and rights-erosive reform pushed despite criticism.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| México | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico | The Reuters Institute says Gálvez obtained a court-ordered right of reply to AMLO’s false claims. That is limited positive evidence that courts could still constrain the president, though it reflects judicial independence more than AMLO’s own strengthening of it. | 4B.4, 4B.3 |
| Presidente alista carpeta de información para familiares de 43 normalistas de Ayotzinapa | Presidencia de México | 2024-07-04 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/presidente-alista-carpeta-de-informacion-para-familiares-de-43-normalistas-de-ayotzinapa/ | The government said it had searched 251 sites, handled 141 cases, and was still working the Ayotzinapa case with families. This is limited positive evidence of continued investigative activity and some accountability channel maintenance, but not broad strengthening of oversight institutions. | 4B.4, 4B.8 |
| Tribunal Electoral valida elección presidencial: Segob; presidente celebra ejemplar transición en gobierno federal | Presidencia de México | 2024-08-13 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/tribunal-electoral-valida-eleccion-presidencial-segob-presidente-celebra-ejemplar-transicion-en-gobierno-federal/ | After the electoral tribunal validated the presidential election, AMLO’s government publicly celebrated an “ejemplar transición.” This is procedural respect for an independent electoral/judicial institution, but it is indirect evidence rather than proof of institutional strengthening. | 4B.4, 4B.1 |
| Mexico constitutional reforms more likely with super-majority in sight | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-04 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexico-constitutional-reforms-more-likely-with-supermajority-in-sight-3469906 | Reuters reported AMLO frequently lambasted the INE and pushed an overhaul critics said could cement Morena’s political hegemony and lower the bar for referendums. This is strong negative evidence on respect for independent electoral oversight. | 4B.4, 4B.1, 4B.2 |
| México’s sweeping judicial overhaul formally takes effect | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-15 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexicos-sweeping-judicial-overhaul-formally-takes-effect-3616588 | Reuters reported AMLO’s judicial overhaul was formally enacted amid criticism that it weakened judicial independence. This is direct negative evidence against strengthening courts that could constrain him. | 4B.4, 4B.2 |
| Mexico proposed constitutional changes threaten rights | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-30 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights | HRW warned the proposed constitutional changes could weaken judicial independence, expand military power, and erode privacy/transparency safeguards. That is broad negative evidence on oversight institutions and counterweights. | 4B.4, 4B.2, 4B.8 |
| Mexico | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico | HRW says civilian killings by the army were rarely independently investigated, and that military obstruction impeded Ayotzinapa and other abuse inquiries. This is strong negative evidence that oversight institutions were not effectively strengthened when they confronted state power. | 4B.4, 4B.8, 4B.9 |
| México | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico | The Reuters Institute describes AMLO’s final year as marked by continued verbal attacks on journalists, human-rights advocates, and the media. That is adverse background evidence for a political climate hostile to independent scrutiny. | 4B.4, 4B.3 |

**Search gap:** I found little direct 2024 evidence that AMLO strengthened legislatures, audit bodies, or local governments. The clearest available material is instead about courts and electoral oversight, and most of that is negative.
